tools.name: check_design
tools.description: Check a page's HTML/CSS/copy/interaction for the patterns that make AI-generated work read as generic: default fonts, soft tech gradients, pill+arrow buttons, eyebrow labels, a composition with no real width/background variation across sections, uniform card grids, copy tells (AI vocabulary, negative-parallel framing, hedge words, heavy em-dash use), and experience gaps (a diagnosis with no next step, dead-end links). Every finding includes a concrete fix. Call this before presenting UI to a human.

html.description: Raw HTML/CSS to check directly, if not fetching a URL

tools.title: Check design

tools.name: check_copy
tools.description: Check marketing or outreach copy (an email, a landing-page draft, a pitch, a social post) for the tells that make it read as AI-generated: cliché vocabulary (delve, unlock, empower, seamlessly integrate, etc.), negative-parallel framing ("not just X, but Y"), hedge words, heavy em-dash use, and diagnosing a problem with no fix in the same breath. No page or markup needed, just the text. Call this before sending copy to a human.
tools.title: Check copy

tools.name: check_code
tools.description: Check a source file or diff for AI 'tells' left in comments: narrating fulfilling a request instead of describing the code ("as requested," "I've added," "here's the updated version") and hedge words. These reveal there was a conversation behind the change that a later reader has no access to. Call this before committing or shipping code an agent wrote.

code.description: The source file or diff to check

tools.title: Check code comments
